newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FEDSURE BUYS STAKE IN IRISH LIFE FIRM.
newsitem.headline: FEDSURE BUYS STAKE IN IRISH LIFE FIRM.

text.p: South African financial services group Fedsure Ltd said on Wednesday it had bought a 25 percent stake in Irish Life International (ILI) for an undisclosed sum.
ILI is a unit of Irish Life, Ireland's largest life assurance, pension and investment group. Fedsure also said it had secured an option to buy a further 15 percent of ILI at the end of 2001.
"The agreement marks a significant step in the development of Fedsure's international activities," Fedsure said in a statement.
Fedsure made its first move abroad earlier this month when it bought a 25.5 percent stake in Isle of Man-based Kingfisher Group.
Fesdure added that it was negotiating a number of other strategic acquisitions and joint-ventures overseas in order to boost its foreign presence.
The move comes as South Africa prepares on July 1 to relax exchange controls on moving funds abroad.

"With the relaxation of exchange controls...it is important for Fedsure to have recognised institutions abroad with whom we can bring new products and investment management skills to the market place," said Fedsure chief executive Arnold Basserabie.
Fedsure joins Irish Life and a private consortium as shareholders in ILI. The private group is headed by ex-South African Monty Hilkowitz.
"Fedsure's expertise in South Africa, which is bound to be an exciting market for international investment business in the future, will greatly enhance our development," Hilkowitz said.
